cards.front: The metabolic demand of an amputation represents the amount of increase in energy expenditure compared to baseline .
cards.extra: Notably, this can change based on the etiology. For example, for a traumatic transtibial ambputation, the metabolic demand is increased by 25%, whereas for vascular etiology, the demand is increased by 40%. The general trend is increasing energy requirement for more proximal amputations. Accordingly, transfemoral (68-100%) increases metabolic demand more than any other single amputation. AKA+BKA (118%) and AKA+AKA (>200%) increase metabolic demand by more, but are bilateral.
